comments.text:
More than 100% Claim settlement ration  is seems misleading. The definition of claim settlement ratio is "dividing the number of insurance claims settled(numerator) by the number of insurance claims received(denominator) by the insurance company". If I file five claims under one policy, and all are settled then it would be calculated as 5/5*100 and not as 5/1*100. 
Moreover, in IRDA report, there is no such data which says "Claim Settlement Ratio". 
In IRDA report, "Incurred Claims Ratio (ICR)" is given. Incurred claim ratio refers to the net claims paid by an insurance company as against the net premiums earned. If the ICR of a company is more than 100%, it indicates that the amount of money given away by the company as claim is more than the amount of money collected by the company as premium. For Acko, Motor insurance ICR was 129% in 2018-19 & 97.58% in 2019-20. There is something called Status of Claims in IRDA report. It has given number of claims received and number of claims paid. That will give the perfect calculation of "Claim settlement ration"
